_date: DERIVED from the level number — see game/calendar.ts. Shift 4 is Sunday 7 March.
_verdict_mode: Pass, Warning or Fine. One warning before a fine, always.
_teaching: Clutter and glazing. Part of a HOUSE becomes clickable for the first time, which is a different kind of looking.
briefing: Sunday. Two articles join the list: exterior condition and accumulated junk. Containers have been at the curb on one of these since Wednesday, which the file will show you.
_cameos: Named residents pinned to addresses rather than rolled. Anything not pinned stays random, so the street is still mostly strangers.
_ambient_animals: The animals loose in yards on this shift. Nights are the wild ones; days are the neighbourhood cat.
story: Sunday round. Nobody expects you on a Sunday, which is presumably why the Board schedules one.
Article XII joins the list today: clutter. Neatly stacked material for a live project is not an accumulation. A sofa is.
Article VI as well — exterior condition. Cracked glazing. Dirty is not cracked.

artifact.text: A board review memo. “Your predecessor’s accuracy was 94%. We mention it as a benchmark.”

lots._teaching: Bins out since Wednesday and still out on Sunday — at the address warned for exactly this on Friday. Two facts point the same way and the player has to hold both: the file says warned, the date on the object says four days past the window.

lots._teaching: The clutter decoy: material stacked for a live project is not an accumulation, and it is staged on the driveway, which is where a project actually stages.

decoys.why: Neatly stacked for an active project. R-107 covers accumulation, not storage.

lots._teaching: The window article, on the address the player knows best. Part of the house is the finding, which is a different kind of looking from a thing sitting on the grass.
Two live articles on one lot, both real, and the appliance is on the DRIVEWAY so R-107 is not learned as "junk on grass".
